terms.comment: Our description, on the pattern of Morgan–Owens’s venēnum contrā īnsecta for an insecticide: unguentum is an ointment (see “sunscreen”), culex the mosquito. No reference work we searched (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini) has a word for an insect repellent.

phrases.latin: Vesper est: mox aderunt culicēs. Unguentum contrā culicēs tibi illinam.
phrases.english: It’s evening: the mosquitoes will soon be here. I’ll put some repellent on you.

phrases.latin: Bracchia et crūra unguentō contrā culicēs unge, nē tē mordeant.
phrases.english: Rub repellent on your arms and legs so they don’t bite you.

phrases.latin: malī culicēs rānaeque palūstrēs āvertunt somnōs
phrases.english: the wretched mosquitoes and the marsh frogs keep sleep away

sources: Lewis & Short: unguentum · Lewis & Short: culex · Lewis & Short: illino
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. insecticide.
